directory.heroSubtitle: Produce rigorous NT and OT exegetical papers with morphological, syntactic, and lexical analysis, verified citations, and TMS-style formatting — step by step, not all at once.
directory.newPaperHint: Configure the passage, upload the project-specific corpus extracts, and pick the style guide (once per account).
directory.papersSubtitle: Continue an in-progress paper or start a new one.

empty.title: No papers yet
empty.body: Start by creating your first exegetical paper. We walk you through it step by step: passage, corpus, verse-by-verse generation, conclusion, introduction, and final assembly.

comingSoon.title: v1 under construction
comingSoon.body: This first version focuses on the assisted writing flow: project setup, step-by-step verse generation with interaction, and final assembly. Programmatic citation verification (the real differentiator vs NotebookLM) arrives in the next version.

biblical-text-edition.label: Biblical text edition
biblical-text-edition.description: The original-language text edition you are exegeting.

critical-apparatus.label: Critical apparatus
critical-apparatus.description: Manuscript variants used when the received text is disputed.

lexicon-technical.label: Technical lexicon
lexicon-technical.description: Academic lexicons with full entries, glosses, and semantics.

theological-dictionary.label: Theological dictionary
theological-dictionary.description: Multi-volume dictionaries that treat semantic fields and theological trajectories.

grammar-syntax.label: Grammar / syntax
grammar-syntax.description: Technical grammars to back up syntactic claims.

commentary-critical.label: Critical commentary
commentary-critical.description: Academic exegetical commentaries that engage the original-language text technically.

commentary-expository.label: Expository commentary
commentary-expository.description: Mid-level academic-pastoral commentaries that bridge exegesis to theology.

historical-background.label: Historical/cultural background
historical-background.description: Studies of the historical and cultural setting of the passage.

theological-monograph.label: Theological monograph
theological-monograph.description: Academic books focused on a specific theological topic.
theological-monograph.examples: Bateman on warning passages, Beale on intertextuality

journal-article.label: Journal article
journal-article.description: Peer-reviewed articles reflecting current scholarly debate.

primary-source-ancient.label: Ancient primary source
primary-source-ancient.description: Sources contemporary with the biblical text.

style-template-paper.label: Style template (never cited)
style-template-paper.description: Sample paper the agent imitates in form — never cited inline.

other.label: Other
other.description: A source that doesn't cleanly fit another category. Use sparingly.

create.title: New exegetical paper
create.subtitle: Set the passage and frame the work for the agent. We'll define rubric, sources, and structural plan next.

brief.title: Paper framing
brief.subtitle: What did your professor assign? What angle do you want to take? This guides the agent across EVERY step.
brief.placeholder: Ex: My professor assigned an exegetical analysis of Hebrews 1:1-4 with a Christological focus. I want to argue that the final revelation in the Son establishes the thematic superiority of the epistle.
brief.optional: Optional but strongly recommended. You can edit it later.
brief.tip: The clearer the framing, the more cohesive the paper. Mention the passage, the emphasis (Christological, ecclesiological, etc.), and any explicit professor expectations.

toast.createFailed: Could not create the paper. Please try again.

paperSetup.subtitle: Academic configuration: rubric, style guide, corpus, and structural plan.

notFound.title: Paper not found
notFound.body: We couldn't load this paper. Go back to the list.

rubric.heading: Paper rubric
rubric.description: Upload the seminary's rubric or use the academic TMS default. Sets corpus minimums and structural emphases.
rubric.uploadComingSoon: Uploading the seminary's rubric (PDF) ships in a future version. For now, paste the text below or edit fields manually.

extract.title: Extract rubric from text
extract.subtitle: Paste the rubric or brief your professor gave you. We extract it into a structured form you can review and adjust.
extract.textareaPlaceholder:
Paste the seminary's rubric, the assignment brief, or the professor's instructions.

E.g. 'The exegetical paper must include technical Greek analysis backed by at least two critical commentaries (WBC, NIGTC, etc.), a technical lexicon (BDAG), and a theological dictionary (TDNT/NIDNTTE)...'
extract.tooShort: Text is too short. Paste at least a paragraph with instructions.
extract.confirmReplace: This will replace the current rubric with the extracted version. Your manual edits will be discarded. Continue?
extract.failed: Could not extract the rubric. Check the text or edit manually.
extract.overloaded: Gemini is currently overloaded. Try again in a few seconds — demand spikes are temporary.

confidenceHint.high: The extraction is complete. Still review the key fields.
confidenceHint.medium: The extraction needed some inference. Review requirements and justifications.
confidenceHint.low: The extraction has gaps. We recommend filling in what's missing manually.

metadata.title: General
metadata.titlePlaceholder: e.g. TMS NT800 — Exegetical paper on Hebrews 1:1-4
metadata.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. Exegetical analysis of the Christological prologue, with technical Greek treatment and discussion of the implications for Hebrews' Christology.
metadata.citationStandardPlaceholder: e.g. TMS / Turabian, SBL Handbook, Chicago 17

requirements.title: Corpus requirements
requirements.subtitle: Minimum and maximum sources per type. The Corpus tab uses this for gap detection.
requirements.justificationPlaceholder: Why is this type necessary? This is shown to the student in gap detection.
requirements.empty: The rubric has no requirements. Add at least one or reset to default.
requirements.duplicateError: There is already a requirement for this type. Edit the existing one.

structural.title: Structural recommendations
structural.subtitle: Source types that should be emphasized in each step. Seeds the suggestions in the structural plan.
structural.noExpectation: No specific recommendation for this step.

actions.resetConfirm: This will discard your edits and reapply the TMS default. Continue?

manifest.heading: Style guide manifest
manifest.description: Verify the mechanical rules extracted from your guide (footnotes, ibid, quotation marks). Correct anything before generating.
manifest.placeholderHint: The manifest viewer + citation samples lands in a later commit.
manifest.noGuide: No active guide attached. Upload one from your profile so the manifest can be extracted automatically.

corpus.heading: Paper corpus
corpus.description: Upload extracts specific to this passage with their academic type. We flag what's missing per the rubric.

gap.metBody: {{count}} sources attached — every minimum is satisfied. You can move on to the structural plan.
gap.gapsBody: You are {{missing}} sources short of meeting the rubric. The details below indicate what types to add.
gap.noRubric: No rubric is attached yet. Configure the rubric in the first tab before loading the corpus.

list.title: Attached sources
list.empty: No sources yet. Upload the first extract below.

upload.title: Add a source
upload.typeDescription: Pick the type that best describes the source. The rubric uses this type to decide whether it satisfies minimums.
upload.citationKeyHint: Used in footnotes. Leave empty and we derive it from the corpus.
upload.modelPaperHint: Style templates are used as form models only. They are NEVER cited inline.
upload.labelTooShort: Label is too short (3 characters minimum)

toast.addFailed: Could not add the source. Please try again.

plan.heading: Structural plan
plan.description: For each step (intro, verse, conclusion) confirm or adjust which source types the agent should prioritize. Suggestions come from the rubric.

kindDescription.introduction: Written last but appears first. Frames the thesis and positions the passage.
kindDescription.verse: Verse-by-verse analysis: translation, morphology, syntax, source interaction.
kindDescription.conclusion: Synthesizes accepted analyses without introducing new arguments.

plan.rubricEmpty: The rubric has no emphasis for this step. Pick the types that fit your paper.
plan.noRubric: No rubric attached yet. Configure the rubric first to see academic suggestions.
plan.emphasizedTypesHint: The agent cites these types generously in this step.
plan.deemphasizedTypesHint: These appear only briefly, without leading the argument.
plan.notePlaceholder: e.g. 'For verses I want strong lexical emphasis because translation decisions carry the argument.'
plan.noteHint: Your reasoning is preserved for later reference.
plan.neverSaved: You have not saved a custom plan yet. The rubric applies as the active suggestion.

setup.title: New exegetical paper
setup.subtitle: Configure the passage, the style guide, and the project-specific corpus.

passage.stepSubtitle: Pick the biblical range to study. Validated against the canon (66 books) on the spot.
passage.helperHint: Supports abbreviations, accents, and both separators (Heb 1:1 / Heb 1.1).

styleGuide.stepSubtitle: Once per user. If you have an active one it's auto-selected; otherwise upload it here.
styleGuide.extractionHint: PDF processing (LlamaParse) continues in the background. The guide is registered immediately; if extraction hasn't finished by the time you try to generate, we'll tell you.

toast.uploadFailed: Couldn't upload the guide. Please try again.

sources.stepSubtitle: Extracts specific to this passage. Each tagged with a role — the orchestrator honors those roles when citing.
sources.scopeHint: Sources here are specific to this paper. You can promote one to your general library later (coming soon).
sources.modelPaperHint: Model papers are used as a STYLE template only. They are NOT cited inline.

toast.uploadFailed: Couldn't upload the source. Please try again.
toast.attachFailed: Paper was created but some sources weren't attached. You can add them from the detail page.

toast.createFailed: Couldn't create the paper. Please try again.

detail.stepsSubtitle: Verse by verse, conclusion, introduction, and assembly. You accept or regenerate each step before moving on.

stepsEmpty.title: No steps generated yet
stepsEmpty.body_one: We'll produce 1 step per verse ({{verseCount}}) plus conclusion, introduction, and assembly.
stepsEmpty.body_other: We'll produce 1 step per verse ({{verseCount}}) plus conclusion, introduction, and assembly.
stepsEmpty.body: We'll produce one step per verse of the passage, plus conclusion, introduction, and final assembly.

steps.failedHint: Something failed while generating this step. Try again.
steps.editHint: Manually edited — citation verification does NOT auto-run.
steps.hintPlaceholder: e.g. more syntax, more theology, cite Cockerill more

gate.multiChapter: v1 only supports single-chapter passages. Edit the passage to a single chapter to start.
gate.noVerses: v1 requires explicit verses. Edit the passage to include start and end verses.

toast.seeded: Steps created — start with the first one
toast.seedShapeError: Passage doesn't qualify for v1 (must be a single chapter with explicit verses)

styleGuide.none: No guide attached. Required before generating.
